facts.fact: The PROGOUV terms of reference of February 2024 state that the civil-status centres of Djibouti city's three communes and five maternity antennas record civil-status events in the city's computerised system SIGEC, whose data sit on a central server in a room of the town hall.
facts.system: SIGEC entry from the commune civil-status centres to the central server at the hôtel de Ville

facts.fact: The PROGOUV terms of reference of February 2024 count three commune civil-status centres working in SIGEC, one in each of Djibouti city's three communes (Balbala, Ras Dika, Boulaos), with five antennas in health facilities; all are in the capital and no total of local governments nationally is given.
facts.system: SIGEC entry from the commune civil-status centres to the central server at the hôtel de Ville

systems.system: Système informatisé de gestion de l'état civil (SIGEC)
systems.platform: software developed by the Société de Développement des Systèmes d'Information (SDSI); central server in the hôtel de Ville
systems.owner: Ville de Djibouti (Mairie); the administrator is a former SDSI technician
systems.tiers: the Mairie's central civil-status centre (housed at the interior ministry's DGPF), three commune centres and five antennas in health facilities, all in Djibouti city; in use since 2011

systems.system: SIGEC entry from the commune civil-status centres to the central server at the hôtel de Ville
systems.tiers: three commune civil-status centres and five antennas, Djibouti city only

note: The connection is read from staff of the commune centres working in a shared system held on the town hall's server; the document does not describe the link itself or who pays for it, so no 'connected' or governance fact is taken. The parent should check that reading. The EUR 8 million PROGOUV funds the diagnostic and capacity building, not a connection.
